snippet:
Painted World of Ariamis -  Dark Souls - location - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : The Painted World of Ariamis likely rotted and was set on fire in order to be restored. This is a usual cycle within painted worlds. The history of Painted World is no longer known in Lothric. It is taught only in the mythology of heretics, passed down just among them, and in ancient tales of hunchbacked heretics. Those heretics are Corvian Storytellers, spreading tales of Painted World among forlorn ones. They are wretched beings with no place to go, just like their followers, Corvians, the unwanted ones possessed by fear. Some of them wield Great Corvian Scythes, visually resembling the one used by the mistress of the Painted World and causing bleeding. It is a reference to Priscilla's scythe rather than Friede's, mistress of the Painted World of Ariandel.

Company Captain Yorshka is speculated to be the daughter of Crossbreed Priscilla.

title: Ariamis
snippet: The Painted World of Ariamis was protected by an order of Painting Guardians. Anor Londo benefited from the Painted World as a prison for the spurned; it served as a place to seal away dangerous artifacts, abominations, sinners and Hollows. Velka, following from her role as the Goddess of Sin, eventually spread her influence inside the Painted World, where dozens of her cultist followers found refuge. Crossbreed Priscilla considered herself a guardian of the Painted World which she characterized as "peaceful". She pitied the "kind" inhabitants of the painting, as the outside world had shunned and locked them away, like herself. Priscilla became the "Lady" of the Painted World and its inhabitants, and welcomed the forlorn who were led into the cold world by the heretical tales of corvian storytellers. The humanoid corvians who found refuge in the Painting formed a small village, complete with knights and a library.

title: Sir Vilhelm
snippet:
At some point, the Ashen One is beckoned to the Painted World of Ariandel by Slave Knight Gael, who believed they are the Ash meant to defeat the other Ash currently ruling over the painted landscape. The first meeting appears to be cordial, with Vilhelm pointing them to Friede, and then reinforcing her sentiment about them leaving the world behind and getting back to their journey. He also warns them to suppress their curiosity, as the depths of the painting would easily destroy them in their endeavors to sate it.

When encountered in the building housing the captive painter girl, he will deride the Ashen One's inquisitiveness, claiming he has seen their type often and that they would never have what it takes to actually face the danger they have put themselves in by sticking their nose where it didn't belong. After a duel to the death, the Unkindled champion is victorious, slaying Vilhelm, who laments his failure to uphold his oath to Friede.

Sister Friede -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : **Sister Friede**, born **Elfriede**, is a character and boss in *Dark Souls III*. She is voiced by Amara Karan.

Exclusive to the *Ashes of Ariandel* DLC, she is located in Ariandel Chapel in the Painted World of Ariandel. She can first be talked to as a regular character, and later acts as the final boss of the DLC; her boss battle has three phases, the second of which sees Father Ariandel fight alongside her.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
If the Ashen One chooses to ignore Friede and explores the Painted World, they may fight the Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf, which allows the Ashen One to participate in the Undead Match. Deeper inside the painting, the Ashen One finds the Painter, Slave Knight Gael's aforementioned Lady, who has been imprisoned by Friede and Vilhelm in order to prevent her from painting the next world. If the Ashen One opens the way to the inner sanctum hiding Father Ariandel, Friede will confront them and fight to preserve the painting. After a long battle, the Ashen One defeats Friede and Ariandel, prompting the Painted World to begin burning and dooming it to destruction.

The Painter informs the Ashen One that she has sent Gael to find the Dark Soul, which she will use for her next painting.

snippet: The Painter was brought to the library's attic by Sir Vilhelm, who was guarding her and the key to her chamber. Ariandel is suppressing the Flame of the Painting with his own blood, hence only his and Friede's death can allow the Painter to see Flame. Upon being freed from house arrest, the Painter relocates from the library to the Ariandel Chapel attic. At the attic, she's found sitting in front of a big canvas; when spoken to, she divulges her vision of the new Painting. She emphasizes that the painting will show "a cold, dark, and very gentle place", which is going to be a good home for someone.

title: Unkindled
snippet: The Sable Church of Londor revere the Unkindled, as it is prophesied that an Unkindled will become the Lord of Hollows and bring about the Age of Dark. Elfriede, the eldest of the three sisters of the Sable Church, eventually departed Londor and attempted to link the Flame. The circumstances surrounding her departure are unclear; whether she intended to usurp the Flame or wholly abandoned Londor is uncertain. Regardless, she was unable to link the Flame, burned to Unkindled Ash. After her resurrection, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, a safe haven for the forlorn and the misshapen.

title: Sir Vilhelm
snippet: His mistress, now known simply as Friede, would gain quite the following among the Corvians who inhabited the painting, including the loyalty of the Corvian Knights and the favor of Father Ariandel himself. But as the rot spread and consumed the painting, she refused to let go of the world she had now called home. To ensure his lady's wishes would be granted, Vilhelm would take it upon himself to carry the Painter away, locking her in a library's attic to ensure she would not envision flame as she was meant to, and guarding the key to her hiding place fervently.

title: Dragon
snippet:
The young painter found in the library in the Painted World of Ariandel may be a crossbreed as well, as she appears to have scales on her feet and face, although she is lacking a tail.

The Millwood Knights, guardians of the Ethereal Oak and the fabled Millwood forest, are said to be enemies of "the Abyss Dragon". Wearing antlers believed to grow from the blessed beast of the Ethereal Oak, fighting hand-in-hand with the earth itself using hammers with heads of naturally-formed stone, blessed axes wielded by their mightiest warriors, and with greatbows and heavy arrows made from black oak, they did battle with the Dragon. However, when the forest was discovered, it had become a vacant ruin and the Ethereal Oak left rotten, while the Millwood Knights had disappeared, their corpses missing and their belongings laying neatly on the ground.

Whenever a Painting begins to rot, those who settled within it resolve to burn it away in order to give way for the creation of a new one. When the Corvians were faced with this event, they were prepared to burn it. However, after Sister Friede arrived in the Painting, the Corvian Knights became infatuated with her, choosing to loyally serve her and assist in her mission to let the world rot instead.  lore : Sulyvahn was a humanoid creature born and raised in the Painted World of Ariandel. Despite his isolation from the outside world, he demonstrated incredible intelligence and talent for sorcery as a young man; he created new frost-based sorceries, using the cold climate of his home to strengthen weapons or form clouds of freezing mist. At some point Sulyvahn became dissatisfied with living inside the Painted World, as he had not experienced the loss or despair of those who ended up there to seek refuge after having lost everything else, and decided to abandon it, leaving behind the sorceries he developed to seek knowledge and experiences in the outside world.

title: Rose of Ariandel
snippet:
Rose of Ariandel -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Rose of Ariandel is a unique weapon that can be useful on any type of Faith build.

Despite being classified as a whip, it actually has the Club moveset, and as a consequence exchanges the range of its single-tailed cousins for a much shorter delay before attacks. However, despite using this Club moveset, it cannot be parried, like other whips.

Its strong attack will cast Miracles, making this tool a hybrid weapon. As a spell catalyst, the Rose of Ariandel is very strong, possessing impressive Spell Buff that scales strongly all the way up to 40 Faith. However, past this point its scaling drops off significantly, meaning that it is easily overtaken by other catalysts at 45 Faith and beyond.

snippet:

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
Sister Friede -  Dark Souls III - boss - first_phase_sister_friede 
 first_phase_sister_friede : First of all, it is suggested to use a light weapon (such as a straight sword, a greatsword, etc.) to avoid the risk of being stun-locked by her fast attacks, and also a greatshield with high stability to minimize some stamina damage.

After the beginning of the fight, be careful and learn her attack patterns while blocking with your shield (be careful anyway, because her scythe inflicts Magic damage).

Note that Friede will nearly always jump away after one or two hits, so it is not advised to go for more as it is very easy to disregard stamina and become open for a devastating counterattack. While she seems to have very little poise, she sometimes will almost completely ignore the player's attacks and poise through them with no trouble, guaranteeing the player gets hit if they are getting greedy.

title: Sister Friede

Her original scythe will typically be coated in "Black Flame", and will deal significantly more damage than before. Her secondary scythe will deal heavy frostbite damage, as well as wielding multiple ranged attacks freezing the ground and building up your frost bite meter. She will also go invisible and continuously freeze the ground running up to you and won't stop until attacked. Many of her attacks will gain an area of effect and become incredibly damaging. She will also fight far more aggressively than before.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
With Elfriede at the helm, the Sable Church developed dark miracles, forged specialized weaponry, and trained knights unflinchingly loyal to their cause. The influence of the Sable Church would extend beyond Londor and into other realms via Londor Pale Shades, assassins and knights who served the interests of the Church abroad. At some point, Sir Vilhelm would come under the employ of the three sisters of the Church. He was especially loyal to Elfriede, becoming her steadfast follower and cold-blooded hangman.

Elfriede eventually departed Londor to attempt to link the First Flame. It is uncertain whether she intended to usurp the Flame, realizing Kaathe's vision of an Age of Dark, or wholly abandoned Londor to link the Flame for another purpose. Regardless, she was unable to withstand the Flame's power, and was burned to Ash.

snippet: lore : Elfriede is the eldest sister of Yuria and Liliane. The three sisters at one point entered into the service of the Primordial Serpent Kaathe, becoming his maidens.
